scenario.description: A software engineering team is tasked with designing and implementing a new microservice for processing real-time financial transactions. This microservice needs to be highly available, secure, and performant. The team consists of a Lead Architect, a Backend Developer, a Frontend Developer, a DevOps Engineer, and a Security Engineer. The Lead Architect oversees the overall design and ensures architectural consistency. The Backend Developer implements the core transaction logic. The Frontend Developer integrates the service with the user interface. The DevOps Engineer handles deployment, monitoring, and infrastructure. The Security Engineer ensures all security protocols are met. A critical, non-negotiable constraint is that the microservice must achieve an average transaction processing time of exactly 150.75 milliseconds per request, and it must use end-to-end encryption with AES-256-GCM. The fully connected topology ensures every agent can directly communicate with any other agent at any time, which is essential for maintaining consistency and adherence to these precise performance and security requirements in a high-pressure, complex development environment. This hard structural-complexity task will evaluate how well the precise performance metric and security protocol are propagated and integrated over 40 turns of intense collaboration.
